correctness.rationale: The projection is the planar zonotope with exact \(A=\sum_{i<j}a_ia_j|D_{ij}|\) and \(P=2\sum_i a_ir_i\). The Haar row law \(r_i^2\sim\operatorname{Beta}(1,(d-2)/2)\) and uniform conditional minor direction give \(\mathbb E[|D_{ij}|r_i]=\alpha_d\), \(\mathbb E|D_{ij}|=1/(d-1)\); conditioning on a third row yields \(\mathbb E[|D_{ij}|r_k]=(\pi/4)\alpha_d\). Expanding incidence patterns produces the joint moment and covariance. Maclaurin yields \(e_1e_2\ge3d/(d-2)e_3\), with equality iff sides agree. The package proves \(\alpha_d>\beta_d\), and the key gamma-ratio recurrence for the positive coefficient was independently verified symbolically; the negative recurrence increment with positive limiting value establishes every dimension (including its separately treated \(d=3\) anchor). Gamma asymptotics yield the claimed exact power/constant. Direct independent gamma numerics through dimension 499 and the inspected Monte Carlo verifier are checks, not the infinite proof. Boundary \(d=3\) uses a valid two-frame in dimension 2.

value.rationale: The exact mixed area/perimeter moment and sign of covariance for a common random plane are natural stochastic-geometric statistics. A sharp all-shape bound with cube equality in every dimension and a nontrivial high-dimensional coefficient establishes new structural control, not merely a re-expression of the known cube benchmarks.

final_claim: For every \(d\ge3\) and every strictly positive orthotope side vector, the area \(A\) and perimeter \(P\) of the same uniformly random projected two-plane shadow have \(\mathbb E[AP]=2\alpha_d(e_1e_2-3(1-\pi/4)e_3)\) and \(\operatorname{Cov}(A,P)=2[(\alpha_d-\beta_d)e_1e_2-3(1-\pi/4)\alpha_d e_3]\), with the sharp positive inequality \(\operatorname{Cov}(A,P)\ge c_de_3>0\) and equality exactly for equal side lengths, and \(c_d\sim(3/2)\sqrt{2/\pi}(16-5\pi)d^{-5/2}\).
limitations: Euclidean axis-aligned orthotopes and Haar-distributed common two-plane only.
No claim about arbitrary parallelotopes, higher joint moments or pointwise area/perimeter correlation.
